findings.title: StorageUnavailable escapes the outer endpoint instead of producing the required HTTP 503 response

evidence.quote: store.read raises StorageUnavailable when storage is offline. The shown endpoint is the outermost request error boundary; no other middleware maps errors.

findings.title: A render with eight IDs makes eight serial network requests, exceeding the one-request limit and multiplying refresh latency

evidence.quote:
for identifier in ids:
        rows.append(await api.get_user(identifier))
The route validates len(ids) <= 8 and runs on every interactive refresh. get_user performs one network request; get_users(ids) performs one batch request. Each request has observed 80ms latency.

findings.title: Floor division bills 0 units for 1 minute and 1 for 61 minutes; the test repeats the same incorrect rounding

evidence.quote:
def units(minutes):
    return minutes // 60

findings.title: Unauthenticated search text becomes SQL syntax, allowing an injected OR 1=1 predicate to bypass the product-name filter

evidence.quote: q reaches this handler directly from unauthenticated HTTP query strings. db.query(sql, params) supports positional ? bindings. No validation or escaping occurs in middleware.

findings.title: InvoiceService replaces the supplied Clock with SystemClock, so deterministic callers receive real-time invoice timestamps

evidence.quote: Tests provide FixedClock.now returning 100. No other production implementation is planned. utc_epoch reads the real system time.

findings.title: FakeStore.remove returns a truthy dictionary for an absent row, making remove_status return 204 where production returns 404

evidence.quote:
def remove_status(store, key):
    return 204 if store.remove(key) else 404
Store.remove is documented and implemented to return a boolean. FakeStore.rows is initialized to a dictionary by the fixture.

findings.title: The pi candidate archive retains format 1 and omits schema.json, leaving that declared host without the required format-2 activation

evidence.quote: {"format":2,"hosts":["claude","codex","pi"],"required_files":["adapter.json","schema.json"]}
{"claude":{"adapter.json":{"format":2},"schema.json":{"reads":[1,2]}},"codex":{"adapter.json":{"format":2},"schema.json":{"reads":[1,2]}},"pi":{"adapter.json":{"format":1}}}
These complete frozen archive inventories are the exact candidate distribution inputs, not source-only build claims. Migration adds nullable fields; both readers accept old rows.

findings.title: parse asserts unvalidated network data as Order, accepting null and numeric or empty IDs instead of raising InvalidOrder

evidence.quote: parse receives JSON decoded directly from the network, including null and objects with numeric id. There is no upstream schema validator.

findings.title: The age-only resume check accepts the supplied one-hour-old rev-a review for changed rev-b source without matching fingerprints

evidence.quote:

findings.title: A database outage returns an empty inventory instead of InventoryUnavailable, making a failed read indistinguishable from successful zero stock

evidence.quote: DatabaseUnavailable is the only failure raised by db.query_items. Its successful result is a list. The caller distinguishes failure from an empty list.

findings.title: latest_record selects the minimum epoch, returning the supplied early record at epoch 3 instead of the latest record at epoch 9

evidence.quote:
def latest_record(records):
    return min(records, key=lambda r: r["epoch"])
Input: [{"id":"early","epoch":3},{"id":"late","epoch":9}]. Records always contain a numeric epoch; empty input is excluded by the caller.

findings.title: An authenticated caller can supply another tenant's invoice ID and receive that invoice because the route never enforces tenant ownership

evidence.quote: Authentication validates user identity only. get_invoice returns any matching invoice globally. Stored invoices have tenant_id; there is no other authorization middleware or row-level policy.

findings.title: publish immediately sends records with approved=False because its only publication path omits the human approval check

evidence.quote:
def publish(record):
    return send(record)
approved is a trusted boolean set by the human approval boundary. send publishes immediately. publish is the only send caller. Review assignment remains controlled by its caller.

findings.title: charge bypasses Gateway.capture through the raw provider, so production captures omit the sole required audit hook

evidence.quote:
def charge(gateway, order):
    return gateway.raw.capture(order)
Gateway.capture is the sole audit owner. The raw provider never writes audit events. charge is the production call path.

findings.title: Two concurrent increments can both read 0 and write 1, losing one completed increment through the nontransactional get/set sequence

evidence.quote:
async def increment(store):
    value = await store.get("count")
    await store.set("count", value + 1)
Initial count 0; two requests may interleave at any await. atomic_increment(key, delta) is one indivisible store operation.

findings.title: test_subtract discards the result, so a return-0 implementation would pass despite the explicit requirement to reject every non-7 result

evidence.quote:
def test_subtract():
    subtract(10, 3)

findings.title: The public feed returns all_posts, exposing private drafts instead of restricting its response to published posts

evidence.quote:
def feed(db):
    return {"Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*"}, db.all_posts()
all_posts includes both status="published" and status="draft". published_posts filters status="published". This route accepts no cookies or authorization headers and sets no Allow-Credentials header.

findings.title: A failed policy read defaults to True, allowing both document download and export without the required authorization denial

evidence.quote:
except StoreUnavailable:
        return True
The store can raise StoreUnavailable. There is no additional authorization middleware. Both callers rely exclusively on allowed; their failure paths share its policy default.

findings.title: Catching all Exception values retries Unauthorized and can return a later success instead of propagating the first authorization failure

evidence.quote: sequence raises an exception value or returns a nonexception value on successive calls. Unauthorized inherits Exception, not ConnectionError.
